title: Chase the move/resize stall while a scan starts in SL-039/SL-040's window: A/B de51999 against HEAD on real D:\ in the same batch, then find what blocks the UI thread
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: A/B run of de51999 against HEAD on real D:\, in the same batch: missing
Whether the 860 px default window height worsens the move/resize stall vs 620 px (measured): missing
Root cause identified for what blocks the UI thread during the stall: partial
de51999-runs-under-current-t005: T-005 errors out on de51999: hook finds "no FolderTree" — de51999 predates SL-044's tree UI
only-width-differs-de51999-to-head: Criterion met: 33 files, +3185/-438 lines touch scan-start, refresh, worker pool, store publishing

Does 'real D:\' in this slice's brief mean T-005's synthetic 100,000-file tree redirected onto D:\ (what this design measures, and what reproduced the stall 18/18 in spike 5), or an actual scan of whatever is really on the D:\ drive (what SL-044's earlier validate run may have done)? The workload and memory profile differ, and the design proceeds on the former reading without a person confirming it's what the epic meant.

If the unelevated EventPipe attribution hits its ceiling (CANNOT-READ, or a wait that resolves only to native code with no managed caller), should an elevated ETW/WPR capture be authorized for this one diagnostic session? The project runs the shipped app unelevated by constraint, but this is a one-off investigation of the app, not the app itself, and going further is a call for a person, not a default this design can make on its own.
FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG, the in-process fallback, exists only as a contract. No Trace batch reached cannot-read or tracing-masks.

I did not re-run trace-2 and render-2 under the new sizing. Every run was at 860 px, where the old height set did nothing, and the one move at load was the same in both arms. Their 860 px first-move stall (333.6-343.9 ms) matches height-850-2's (334.3-346.8 ms).
A scan of D:\'s real contents and an elevated ETW/WPR capture remain open questions for a person (design-slice).
Run a Render batch of 8 pairs. render-2's 4 pairs could only have detected a 5.41x difference, so whether the SyncFlush wait is GPU- or present-side is not settled.

Measure where the first resize's cost goes when the window is resized once before it is shown, for example with a probe from before the window loads. In height-3 and height-850 that resize removed the ~340 ms from the hook's first move, which makes it the fix candidate this slice points to; nothing measured startup.
Run a traced batch of the ~1.3 s stall (the brief's 1,318.5 ms). In this attempt's batches it was the largest wait in 5 to 12 of 16 runs, in both arms, in the scan or the rescan.

Loop note: this is the third build attempt sent back over where the hook sets the height (M1, M3, and this attempt's own SourceInitialized version). This time the control batch (860 vs 850, height-850-2) settles it by measurement; a reviewer can check its runs rather than reason about WPF's event order.

D:\fsa-sl080-temp is still in place, as in attempt 1. artifacts/sl080 holds the superseded height-1/2/3 and height-850 batches beside height-4 and height-850-2 (gitignored; the doc marks which are superseded).
The code-review drift items not taken up here (the symmetric orderEffect flag; the Render rule's missing power floor) are still recorded under code-review.

not reached: The GC-share result is conditional on heaps up to ~110 MB. A real multi-GB scan's rescan stall was not checked for GC share.
